title: Small discrete problems: CPU torch, CUDA torch, fused CUDA, streamed and reversible forward and VJP agreement

fixture.native_forward: tests/test_solver.py: 40x40x1 (2d) and 40x40x40 (3d) cells, 180 steps, float32 and float64, CPU NumPy backend against CUDA torch kernel with and without CUDA graphs
fixture.fused_kernels: tests/test_cuda_kernels.py: random E, H, inverse epsilon and all CPML psi states (seed 615) on 32x28x1 or 32x28x24 cells with pml2d, pml3d, mixed and graded CPML layouts, 23 steps, float32 and float64, CUDA torch YeeGrid against FusedYeeCUDA; complete fused graph 40x30x1 cells, 180 steps, dielectric and Lorentz; subnormal fields; CPU float64 Simulation against fused CUDA frequency plane on 320x20x40 cells, 1600 steps
fixture.fused_adjoint: tests/test_cuda_adjoint.py: random physical and adjoint states (seed 82) on the 16x15x14 project of tests/test_differentiable.py, 3 transposed steps, float32 and float64, FusedAdjointCUDA.step against _System.transpose_step
fixture.explicit_adjoint: tests/test_differentiable.py: 16x15x1 and 16x15x14 cells, 24 steps, float64, seed 82 epsilon and weights, checkpoints 3, cpu and cuda, explicit adjoint against full autograd
fixture.tensor_native: tests/test_tensor_native_cuda.py: 16x6x6 cells, 12 steps, float32, periodic, Bloch and CPML, CPU against CUDA forward and material-table VJP
fixture.endpoint_cpml: tests/test_endpoint_native_cpml_cuda.py: 16x6x6 nodes, 20 steps, float32, CPU against CUDA forward, interior epsilon and waveform VJPs
fixture.streamed: tests/test_spacetime.py: SlabBlockOperator forward and transpose on 16x15x14 cells with temporal depths 1, 3, 9 and local checkpoints, float32 and float64, cpu and cuda, against the host reference step by autograd (seed 608); tests/test_streamed_density.py: CPU dense resident reference against CUDA asynchronous streamed periodic density response and gradient, float32; tests/test_pec_boundaries.py: 2D 16x16 PEC scene, resident (fused on CUDA) and streamed against the reference, real and complex
fixture.all_modes_driver: tests/test_cpu_gpu_adjoint_benchmark.py via benchmarks/cpu_gpu_adjoint.py: 16^3 cells, 19 steps, float32, x periodic, two plane monitors, modes cpu_t1, cpu_t2 (torch backward), cuda_resident (fused) and cuda_dram (streamed async), dielectric and dispersive, every mode's outputs and material VJPs against cpu_t1 by relative L2
fixture.reversible: tests/test_reversible.py: 6^3 periodic cells, 80 and 512 steps, float32 CPU, reversible backward against the stored full gradient, two random cotangent seeds (generator 37) and a central difference; tests/test_reversible_cuda.py: fused CUDA reversible on 12^3 x 96 steps and 64^3 x 512 steps (generator 74)
fixture.pml: CPML layers 3 to 4 in the differentiable fixtures; pml2d/pml3d/mixed/graded layouts in the kernel test; part of the compared operator

reference_method: The same discrete problem executed through another path of the same Yee/CPML discretisation: NumPy or torch CPU against CUDA torch, torch against fused CUDA kernels, explicit transpose against torch autograd, resident against streamed or reversible execution. No path is independent of the discrete operator; this is validation layer A only.

observables.name: forward_fields_and_signals
observables.definition: E, H, CPML psi and monitor signals of one path against another after N steps

observables.name: material_vjp
observables.definition: adjoint or backward gradients with respect to epsilon, density, tensor table or waveform of one path against another

observables.name: adjoint_states
observables.definition: transposed E, H and psi bars of the fused adjoint against the torch transpose

observables.name: relative_l2
observables.definition: per-group relative L2 of outputs and VJPs in the all-modes driver and the reversible tests

looser_than_program_thresholds.note: float32 gradient budgets of 2e-4 to 3e-4 relative were declared in the repository before this case for accumulated 12 to 512 step backward passes; they exceed the program's float32 rtol 1e-4 and are reported as differences, not loosened or tightened here; the float32 atol values in absolute reduced units are 2e-7 to 7e-6 against the program's 1e-6

acceptance.source_of_limits: completion_gates.json proposed_thresholds discrete_dimensionless_fp32 and fp64; each test's own assertions are the recorded criteria

not_yet_covered: one fixture compared across all four of CPU torch, CUDA torch, fused CUDA and streamed at once (the driver compares three; the CUDA torch kernel is compared separately)
float32 gradient agreement at the program's rtol 1e-4 on the fixtures whose recorded budgets are 2e-4 to 3e-4

error_budget.precision_floor: float32 forward 2e-6 to 3e-6 relative after 23 to 180 steps; float32 VJP 2e-5 to 3e-4 relative after 12 to 512 backward steps; float64 1e-13 to 2e-10
error_budget.time_window: 12 to 1600 steps per fixture; not a physics window, since both paths integrate the same number of steps
error_budget.pml: part of the compared operator; CPML psi states are compared directly in the kernel and adjoint tests

notes: Layer A only by definition of the task. No test was added; the tests listed are the repository's existing device and execution-path comparisons on small fixtures, chosen so that every pair (CPU-CUDA forward, CPU-CUDA VJP, torch-fused, resident-streamed, stored-reversible) is covered in both precisions where the fixture supports it. tests/test_reversible_cpml_kernels.py is excluded because its CUDA instance is gated by TORCHFDTD_RUN_CPML_KERNEL_CUDA_TEST and would skip.
